en: Title: *Buddhastotra Author: *Vasudhārā Source: Cambridge University Library Or.143

Notes: A fragment consisting of approximately two and a half verses from an eight-verse hymn of praise to the Buddha, possibly composed by a female poet. It was penned in a later hand to fill the scribe’s fear of leaving blank space (*horror vacui*) following an excerpt of verses from the *Bodhicaryāvatāra* and the *ye dharmā* formula, which were inscribed in a bold, eleventh-century script. The manuscript otherwise contains portions of the *Grahamātṛkādhāraṇī*, the *Mañjuśrīnāmāṣṭaśataka*, and the beginning of an unidentified *dhāraṇī*.
By him the gift of his head was given more than once, exceeding the size of Mount Meru;
by him many eyes were also given, surpassing the stars;
and his own flesh, greater even than the earth, and his blood, more than the ocean.
Homage always to that Blessed One, the Buddha, the performer of difficult deeds,
by whom the mind— fickle as the waves of a swirling lightning flash— was brought under control,
and by whom [beings] were ferried across the great ocean of ignorance.
Homage ever to that Blessed One, the Buddha, the performer of difficult deeds, by whom craving was destroyed like an elephant and the Māras were utterly shattered.
Homage to him who bears the burden of the world.
He who obtained for his beloved a boon inaccessible even to the gods,
